To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the throughput of a two-processor organization depends on the organization, and that a dynamically reconfigurably two-processor organization may be a better alternative.

(1) for a given workload, the throughput of a system with two processors is higher than the throughput of a single processor system and (2) for a given throughput requirement, a system with two independent processors has a higher workload capability than a system with two dependent processors.

the performance of a two-processor organization is dependent on the manner in which the processors are connected and that the best performance is achieved by a system that can dynamically reconfigure itself to suit a particular workload.

the performance of a two-processor organization.
the performance of parallel computers.
the study of the throughput and response time of four two-processor organizations under various workloads.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the two-processor organization is a function of the relative values of the mean service time and mean interarrival time.
the two-processor system with a single buffer is the most efficient system for a large range of workloads.
the two-processor organization which has the best performance is the one which is organized as a tandem queue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the two-processor organizations are not significantly different in performance, and the performance is not significantly affected by the manner of organization, provided the organization is not too complex.

the throughput of a parallel processor organization is not a function of the number of processors alone, but is a function of the organization itself.
a two-processor organization is not necessarily better than a two-queue organization.
